vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and a file-based harness for Cursor and Claude Code. THE HARNESS IS: a durable, file-system task system that keeps AI agents honest across sessions. It solves five problems the owner identified: (1) repository scope — vision, direction, trade-offs in state.json; (2) task definition — discrete tasks with type and scope; (3) task grouping — flat tasks[] array filtered by status at read time; (4) task status tracking — lifecycle enum + append-only breadcrumbs.jsonl for session recovery; (5) acceptance criteria — contract.json with binary-testable criteria negotiated before implementation. For whom: teams using Cursor/Claude Code on non-trivial multi-file work who need agents to stop self-grading and stop losing context between sessions. Why each component exists: state.json = scope + backlog; contract.json = definition of done; breadcrumbs = audit trail; planner subagent = decompose vague requests; evaluator subagent = adversarial QA separate from builder context; hooks (lean) = enforce contract-before-code structurally; eval pipeline = regression test that agents follow the workflow. HONEST ASSESSMENT: the core five-problem harness is sound and ~40 lines of JSON + rules. Everything layered on top — negotiations/ JSON schemas, 11 hooks (full profile), metrics dashboard, 31 scenario evals with 5 judge tiers, multi-agent orchestration, UI dashboard — has grown organically and now obscures the value proposition. 47 verified tasks prove the core works; pending tasks are now reprioritized around measurement gaps, not harness failures. ACAM RESEARCH (2026-06-11, COMMITTED): spike-research-agents verified rules-skills as Intermediate on all 4 ACAM dimensions at Tier 3 (~top 0.5% of n≈3,200 public repos). Reaching Advanced requires quantitative effectiveness data — per-rule ablation scores, skill activation eval, CI-integrated eval regression, and measured interaction patterns — not more rules, hooks, or documentation.
direction: STABLE (2026-06-12, updated post-v2): All infrastructure migrations complete. context-package.py and prune-harness.py colocated in library/cursor/hooks/ distributed via make sync-local. harness-context.sh resolves $SCRIPT_DIR/context-package.py. Archive at .harness/.archive/ (gitignored). 270/270 tests + 53/53 hook tests passing, harness_lint 0 errors. ACAM v2 snapshot (2026-06-12): configuration=intermediate, workflows=ADVANCED, multi_agent=intermediate, interaction=intermediate. Tier 3 (~top 0.5%, n=3,200 repos). Measurement loop COMPLETE: feat-acam-static-scorer, chore-eval-baseline-seed, feat-acam-scenario-mapping, docs-eval-measurement-runbook — all committed. v2 tech debt addressed: chore-v2-debt-docs committed, chore-v2-debt-harness in progress. Known acceptable dead code: tests/eval/spike_hooks.py (one-off spike), scripts/clean-harness.sh (nuclear reset, no CI caller). Pending P2: feat-eval-measurement-pass (eval-measure Makefile target), spike-token-estimation, spike-model-selection, spike-token-budget.

trade_offs.decision: Flat tasks array, not grouped buckets
trade_offs.alternative: Group by phase: {backlog, active, done}
trade_offs.reasoning: Hooks and agents iterate one list today; grouped buckets duplicate items and drift. harness-context.sh can filter by status at read time.

trade_offs.decision: Keep lifecycle statuses (pending/building/evaluating/verified/committed)
trade_offs.alternative: User-suggested done/doing
trade_offs.reasoning: Eight lean hooks, harness_lint.py, and 20 eval scenarios already encode this lifecycle. done conflates verified and committed; doing conflates building and evaluating.

trade_offs.decision: Explicit type enum on every task
trade_offs.alternative: Infer type from id prefix only (feat-/gap-/spike-)
trade_offs.reasoning: Id prefixes are convention not validation; explicit type enables lint enforcement and clearer planner output.

trade_offs.decision: Transitional features alias (read-only fallback)
trade_offs.alternative: Big-bang rename in one commit
trade_offs.reasoning: 22+ eval scenario seeds and 6 shell hooks read features today; alias prevents eval regression during phased rollout.

trade_offs.decision: Add cancelled status
trade_offs.alternative: Delete abandoned tasks from array
trade_offs.reasoning: Preserves audit trail; metrics exclude cancelled from backlog counts.

trade_offs.decision: Gitignore entire .cursor/
trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact

trade_offs.decision: Kill spec.md, consolidate into state.json
trade_offs.alternative: Keep spec.md with coherence lint
trade_offs.reasoning: spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.

trade_offs.decision: Cancel feat-13 multi-agent orchestration (2026-06-03) — revisit deferred to feat-13b
trade_offs.alternative: Build evaluator chaining and parallel evaluators
trade_offs.reasoning: At cancellation: manual /evaluator launch works; orchestration adds complexity; no user demand. Revisit triggered (2026-06-11): owner expressed intent to return to programmatic orchestration. feat-13b added to backlog at P3. Pre-requisite: feat-16 ablation data and eval CI (feat-17) should exist first — orchestration without measurement makes it harder to know if it helps.

trade_offs.decision: Cancel spike-2 UI dashboard
trade_offs.alternative: Build canvas/TUI for .harness/ visualization
trade_offs.reasoning: state.json and breadcrumbs are human-readable JSON. Dashboard solves a problem that doesn't exist yet. metrics.json is broken anyway (gap-21).

trade_offs.decision: Defer feat-14 LLM-as-judge until after schema consolidation
trade_offs.alternative: Build LLM judge now to fix UNCERTAIN verdicts
trade_offs.reasoning: 89.8% mean is acceptable. Many UNCERTAIN/FAIL are judge bugs (gap-20 harness_level placement, gap-19 heuristics), not agent failures. Fix tooling before adding LLM cost.

trade_offs.decision: Merge spike-3 into spike-audit-1 simplification
trade_offs.alternative: Separate eval accuracy improvement track
trade_offs.reasoning: Eval accuracy issues are symptoms of schema drift and inconsistent harness_level placement across 41 scenarios. Consolidation fixes root cause.

trade_offs.decision: Keep lean hook profile as default; demote full profile
trade_offs.alternative: Maintain 11 hooks at equal priority
trade_offs.reasoning: Lean (4 hooks) enforces the five-problem core. Full profile adds dedup-server, context-health, evaluator-guard, harness-gate LLM routing — valuable for this repo's dogfooding, optional for consumers.

trade_offs.decision: Make negotiations/ optional, not required
trade_offs.alternative: Enforce structured negotiation JSON per HARNESS_STANDARD.md
trade_offs.reasoning: negotiations/ directory is rarely populated in practice. Breadcrumbs with type=negotiate capture the same signal with less schema burden. HARNESS_STANDARD over-specifies this artifact.

trade_offs.decision: Decompose spike-eval-research into 6 sequential research phases
trade_offs.alternative: Single monolithic research task
trade_offs.reasoning: Four distinct eval dimensions (rules, skills, trajectory, LLM judge) plus baseline inventory and synthesis need focused research passes. Sequential phases produce partial notes that roll into one spike doc without scope creep into implementation.

trade_offs.decision: Consolidate 6 research dimensions into 4 (Configuration, Workflows, Multi-agent, Interaction) + add data collection phase
trade_offs.alternative: Keep 6 separate dimensions (rules, skills, loops, subagents, prompts, system prompts)
trade_offs.reasoning: Builder review identified heavy overlap: rules ARE system prompts; prompts and system prompts are one dimension with sub-layers; skills define workflows within loops. 4 dimensions allow deeper analysis per phase. Separate data collection phase (GitHub scraping, comparable setups) prevents the spike from being pure desk-research opinion.

trade_offs.decision: ACAM uses 3 levels (Basic/Intermediate/Advanced) not 5 (L0-L4)
trade_offs.alternative: 5-level maturity model (L0 Default → L4 Measured)
trade_offs.reasoning: 5-level maturity models (CMMI-style) are notorious for hair-splitting between adjacent levels. 3 levels with clear behavioral markers per dimension are more practical and adoptable. Each level has observable signals, not abstract capability descriptions.

trade_offs.decision: Target: practitioner reference guide, not academic paper
trade_offs.alternative: Aim for academic publication (requires IRB, statistical framework, peer review)
trade_offs.reasoning: The plan has zero empirical data collection methodology, no IRB, no statistical framework. Most impactful AI tooling content is practitioner-oriented. Blog series + conference talk format reaches the target audience directly. Academic rigor can come later with feat-16 ablation data.

trade_offs.decision: Research outputs live in .harness/docs/research/ not docs/
trade_offs.alternative: Publish directly to docs/ for consumer visibility
trade_offs.reasoning: Research is in-progress spike artifacts with bibliography and scorecard JSON; docs/ is consumer-facing standards. Move to docs/ only after synthesis phase validates ACAM and owner approves publication.

trade_offs.decision: Reprioritize measurement infrastructure over new features post-ACAM
trade_offs.alternative: Continue feature development (orchestration, dashboard, new rules)
trade_offs.reasoning: ACAM research confirmed Intermediate on all dimensions with binding constraint: no quantitative effectiveness data. feat-16, chore-skill-scenarios, and feat-17 CI integration unblock Advanced criteria. Adding features without measurement perpetuates the gap the research identified.

trade_offs.decision: Defer context package delivery and prompt versioning to open questions
trade_offs.alternative: Add immediate tasks for structured state bundles and rule changelogs
trade_offs.reasoning: Both are Medium-severity Multi-agent/Interaction gaps. Measurement tasks (ablation, skill eval, CI) are higher leverage and unblock multiple dimensions. Context packages and prompt versioning need design decisions before implementation.

trade_offs.decision: feat-17 tiered CI: 11-scenario protocol PR gate + nightly full suite (31 scenarios)
trade_offs.alternative: Full 27+ scenario suite on every PR
trade_offs.reasoning: Sequential live sessions run ~5–15 min each; full suite is ~4–6 hours and blocks every PR. Protocol-prefix subset (~90–120 min sequential) protects the five-problem harness core; nightly runs all standard + long scenarios with LLM judge tier.

trade_offs.decision: Separate JSONL archives for pruned breadcrumbs and open_questions (not archive.jsonl)
trade_offs.alternative: Append all pruned records to .harness/archive.jsonl with a record_type discriminator
trade_offs.reasoning: archive.jsonl is task-shaped (id, name, status, archived_at) and is read by harness_lint cross-consistency checks. Mixing breadcrumb and question records would break lint assumptions and archive-tasks.py consumers. Dedicated breadcrumbs_archive.jsonl and questions_archive.jsonl keep schemas stable.

trade_offs.decision: Prune is manual or explicit --apply; sessionStart hook emits advisory only
trade_offs.alternative: Auto-prune stale breadcrumbs and resolved questions on every sessionStart
trade_offs.reasoning: Mutating harness state inside sessionStart hooks risks race conditions with concurrent sessions and silent data loss. Matches archive-tasks.py (--dry-run first) pattern. harness-context.sh should surface PRUNE ADVISORY with counts and the command to run, not delete records automatically.

trade_offs.decision: Context package: JSON canonical schema, compact markdown for hook injection
trade_offs.alternative: Markdown-only package or inject raw state.json + contract.json slices
trade_offs.reasoning: JSON is machine-testable (pytest, eval scenarios) and composable for evaluator Task prompts. Markdown is a derived view for token-efficient sessionStart injection. Avoids dumping full builder history while giving evaluator structured task + AC + recent trace.

trade_offs.decision: Colocate hook helper scripts in library/cursor/hooks/ (not scripts/)
trade_offs.alternative: Extend make sync-local to copy scripts/ subset; or add make sync-hooks
trade_offs.reasoning: make sync-local copies library/cursor/hooks/ → .cursor/hooks/ as the only distribution path. Scripts called at sessionStart must live beside the hook that invokes them so $SCRIPT_DIR resolves identically in source and synced copies. Repo-internal tools (archive-tasks.py, migrate-state-schema.py) stay in scripts/.

trade_offs.decision: Four-task measurement loop plan (scorer, baseline seed, scenario mapping, runbook) before P2 token spikes
trade_offs.alternative: Single monolithic 'eval runbook' task covering all deliverables
trade_offs.reasoning: Static ACAM scorer and baseline seeding are independently shippable and unblock regression detection without waiting on live-session mapping or documentation. Runbook comes last so it documents working artifacts, not aspirational procedures.

trade_offs.decision: Defer unified scorecard export to runbook scope (convention + Makefile target) rather than separate feature task
trade_offs.alternative: Dedicated feat-eval-scorecard-export task with new JSON schema and history directory
trade_offs.reasoning: Trend comparison needs a documented snapshot procedure more than a new artifact type. Static ACAM JSON + session summary.json + eval_baseline.json already contain comparable fields once mapping exists; runbook defines how to archive and diff them.

trade_offs.decision: Keep spike-subagent-model-mechanics separate from spike-model-selection
trade_offs.alternative: Fold platform mechanics research into the routing matrix spike
trade_offs.reasoning: Platform mechanics is empirical (needs actual subagent invocations with transcript evidence); routing matrix is desk research + cost analysis. Keeping them separate allows mechanics to run first and feed hard constraints into the matrix, preventing the matrix from making promises the platform cannot keep.

trade_offs.decision: v1 model routing: config + docs only (model: fields in agent files + AGENTS.md), not SDK programmatic dispatch
trade_offs.alternative: SDK-based programmatic role dispatch (feat-13b successor) or hook-enforced automatic switching
trade_offs.reasoning: Config defaults are independently shippable and useful without SDK complexity. Programmatic dispatch requires spike-subagent-model-mechanics to confirm platform support first; hook-enforced switching may not be possible if Cursor does not expose model override APIs at hook time. Ship the known-feasible value first.

trade_offs.decision: eval-model-matrix runs as manual Makefile target + nightly CI, not PR gate
trade_offs.alternative: PR gate for model matrix (blocks every PR on slow matrix run)
trade_offs.reasoning: Matrix runs across 2-4 models x ~4 scenarios; sequential live sessions add significant wall time. Nightly CI provides regression detection without blocking every PR. Matches the precedent set by eval-ci-nightly (31 scenarios) vs eval-ci-pr (11 protocol scenarios).

open_questions: Unresolved: breadcrumb retention policy — keep last N entries (default 50), entries newer than D days (default 7), or whichever retains more? Affects prune-harness defaults and context-health stale-thread thresholds.
Unresolved: vision/direction trim threshold — character limit (e.g. 2000 chars each) vs approximate token budget? prune-harness should preserve first paragraph + last update stamp if trimming.

Unresolved: eval history storage — git-tracked dated snapshots under .harness/eval-history/ vs CI artifacts only vs external dashboard. Runbook should pick one default; implementation can stay manual initially.

Unresolved: PR-tier baseline seed timing — seed eval_baseline.json from first available green run (accepting known behavioral failures in behavioral_baseline) vs wait until skill_activation and session_boundary scores improve. Seeding with known failures enables regression detection on what already passes.

tasks.name: Token footprint audit for harness context
tasks.scope: Measure only — no optimization. Audit token counts for always-on rules, context package output, breadcrumbs, and sessionStart injection using tiktoken or equivalent.
tasks.research_question: How many tokens does the current harness context inject at session start? What's the per-rule, per-breadcrumb, per-context-package token footprint?
tasks.deliverable: scripts/token-audit.py that measures token counts for key artifacts (always-on rules, context package, typical breadcrumbs) using tiktoken or similar

tasks.name: Role-based model routing research (planner / builder / evaluator)
tasks.scope: Research + decision artifacts only — no implementation. Covers: (1) per-role capability requirements and failure modes (planner needs decomposition quality, builder needs code gen, evaluator needs adversarial testing); (2) routing signals (task type, complexity, token footprint from spike-token-estimation, negotiation vs eval mode); (3) platform constraints — Cursor agent frontmatter model: field, inherit behavior, whether subagent Task invocations honor per-agent model, SDK Agent.create(model=) limits, what hooks cannot do; (4) cost/quality trade-offs. Excludes: changing agent files, eval runner code, programmatic auto-dispatch. Soft depends on: spike-token-estimation, spike-subagent-model-mechanics.
tasks.research_question: For each harness role (planner, builder, evaluator), which model tier optimizes outcome-per-cost? What observable signals should drive tier selection, and what does the Cursor platform actually allow?
tasks.deliverable: .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md (narrative + role×tier matrix + anti-patterns) and tests/eval/fixtures/model_routing_matrix.json (machine-readable: role, recommended_tier, fallback_tier, signals, scenarios_to_validate)

tasks.name: Platform spike: subagent model inheritance and eval fidelity
tasks.scope: Empirical platform test only. When builder at model A invokes /planner or /evaluator, which model actually runs? Can eval scenarios meaningfully test role-specific routing, or only builder-model proxy? Document findings for feat-eval-role-model-matrix scope boundaries. Excludes: implementation. Depends on: nothing — can run first.
tasks.research_question: Does Cursor honor per-agent model: on subagent Task invocations, and can our eval sandbox observe it?
tasks.deliverable: Section in model-selection.md + minimal repro notes (transcript evidence from 2-3 manual or scripted sessions)

tasks.name: Investigate: detecting features with zero behavioral change at contract time
tasks.scope: Research + recommendation only — no implementation. Investigate the best mechanism to prevent 'documentation disguised as feature' contracts from passing evaluator negotiation. Root cause: feat-role-model-config was accepted as a feature even though no AC tested changed behavior (model: inherit unchanged). Three candidate approaches to evaluate: (1) Prompt-only — add anti-vacuity rule to evaluator.md ('if no AC tests that something works differently, reject as chore'); (2) Structural/heuristic — a pre-commit or contract-lint check that flags feature contracts where all ACs test file existence/content but none test runtime behavior change; (3) Hybrid — evaluator rule + harness_lint.py static check for feature contracts with only grep/python3 file-existence ACs. Evaluate each on: reliability, false positive rate, implementation cost, whether it degrades valid feature contracts (e.g. doc-only features that are legitimately chores). Depends on: nothing.
tasks.research_question: What is the most reliable and lowest-false-positive mechanism to detect a 'feature' contract where all ACs test file structure rather than behavioral change — at contract negotiation time, before implementation?
tasks.deliverable: .harness/docs/research/vacuous-feature-detection.md with: root cause analysis of feat-role-model-config failure, evaluation of the three candidate approaches, recommendation (prompt / structural / hybrid), and a concrete spec for whichever approach is recommended

tasks.name: Per-task token budget thresholds and enforcement
tasks.scope: Research + proposed spec only — implementation is a separate feature task. Define practical budgets per harness phase and enforcement mechanism.
tasks.research_question: Can we enforce per-task token budgets? What is a practical budget for each harness phase (planning, building, evaluating)?
tasks.deliverable: .harness/docs/research/token-budget.md with proposed budget thresholds and enforcement mechanism
